subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files as part of the core bootstrap context contract?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but broadening startup context injection changes a trusted file-loading and prompt-context boundary that should be intentionally accepted or declined.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow explicit in-workspace custom basenames through the existing bootstrap-extra-files path once the linked PR or a replacement is repaired, documented, and tested against path guards and budgets.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Decline arbitrary workspace-file injection and continue directing users to first-class workspace filenames or documented conventions.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context Design
options.body: Supersede this issue with a broader context API decision if raw configured files are not the permanent contract maintainers want.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow explicit in-workspace custom basenames through the existing bootstrap-extra-files path once the linked PR or a replacement is repaired, documented, and tested against path guards and budgets.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the original hook work and has the clearest history on the boundary-safe file-read contract that this decision would expand.
